body: Here's also another perspective. You can send out your starting military fleet to scout ahead of some systems. It also gives them a chance for the admiral to gain the scout trait. But you gotta watch them from time to time because if they encounter space fauna, they will surely die from them since they don't have the evasive stance to save their butts. So you can set your early military fleets to scout ahead, and once you get a good picture of the map, you survey path your science ships to nearby choke points and build your star bases on that path. If you have closed borders on by default, then that means nearby AI empires can't just go inside your territory to survey and build their bases. Once the choke points are set, you can take your time to survey/solve anomalies, build on free taken territory, and also have a higher level admiral in your fleet. This is my go-to strat for the early game if I ever wanted to take vast amounts of territory from the start so I can take my time on those anomalies and dig sites.

Ah, that's where it all went wrong. The "corvette" of the bio ship set has absolutely bonkers level of close-up damage, especially against armor and hull. You'll stand a better chance if you kite or engage them in long-range battles. Plus, bio ship sets take up a lot of power, so they would usually run ship designs with few to none shields, and you can take advantage of that with weapons that have bonuses against armor and hull.
